html:
The Shasta are a Native American people of northern California and southern Oregon, around the Shasta Valley, the Klamath River and the Scott River. Their language, now no longer spoken in daily life, belongs to the small Shastan family.

They lived in villages of plank houses along the rivers, fished salmon, gathered acorns and hunted deer. They traded with the Karuk downriver and the Modoc to the east. Mount Shasta takes its name from them.

The Gold Rush reached the Klamath country in 1850. Miners took the rivers, and killings and disease cut the Shasta to a fraction of their number in a few years, part of the wider California genocide. Many survivors were moved north after the Rogue River Wars of the 1850s, and others stayed on small rancherias.
